extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a freely and publicly available benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). It contains 31,500 remote sensing images divided into 45 scene classes, with 700 RGB images of size 256×256 pixels in each class, and is designed to provide large scale, rich image variations, and high within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
extraction.creator: Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU)
extraction.citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu. Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art. Proceedings of the IEEE, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by first selecting 45 representative scene classes, then extracting remote sensing images from Google Earth by experts in remote sensing image interpretation. The images were selected under different weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales, and cover more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Remote sensing images extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by superimposing images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) data onto a 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset was extracted, by the experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation, from Google Earth (Google Inc.).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Almost all existing datasets have limitations including small scale of scene classes and image numbers, lack of image variations and diversity, and saturation of accuracy; SIRI-WHU mainly covers urban areas in China and hence lacks diversity and is less challenging; the Brazilian coffee scene dataset has only two scene classes, which is quite small for testing multi-class scene classification methods
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote sensing image scene classification plays an important role in a wide range of applications, such as natural hazards detection, land use and land cover determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: remote sensing image scene classification; develop and evaluate various data-driven algorithms; benchmarking state-of-the-art scene classification methods and providing useful performance baselines for future research
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For the Brazilian coffee scene dataset, the creation of the dataset is performed as follows: tiles with at least 85% of coffee pixels were assigned to the coffee class; tiles with less than 10% of coffee pixels were assigned to the non-coffee class.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For BoVW, BoVW+SPM and LLC methods, we adopted the widely used densely sampled SIFT descriptor to describe each image patch with the patch size set to be 16×16 pixels and the grid spacing to be 8 pixels.
